from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "The Hook: The Morphing Canvas"
        lines = [
            "Imagine Pixel the Cat sitting on a unit grid.",
            "A matrix transformation tilts and stretches the entire space.",
            "Pixel’s shape changes, becoming taller, thinner, or slanted.",
            "The determinant measures the change in Pixel’s total area.",
            "It is the scaling factor for every shape in space."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors for highlights
        color_cat = "#FFFFFF"
        color_grid = "#444444"
        color_area = "#FFFF00"
        color_line_active = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color_line_active))
        
        # Create a simple "Pixel the Cat" character
        cat_head = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        cat_ear_l = Triangle(color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.1).rotate(30*DEGREES).move_to(cat_head.get_top() + LEFT*0.15 + UP*0.05)
        cat_ear_r = Triangle(color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.1).rotate(-30*DEGREES).move_to(cat_head.get_top() + RIGHT*0.15 + UP*0.05)
        cat_eye_l = Dot(radius=0.04, color=BLACK).move_to(cat_head.get_center() + LEFT*0.1 + UP*0.05)
        cat_eye_r = Dot(radius=0.04, color=BLACK).move_to(cat_head.get_center() + RIGHT*0.1 + UP*0.05)
        cat_smile = Arc(radius=0.1, start_angle=200*DEGREES, angle=140*DEGREES, color=BLACK).move_to(cat_head.get_center() + DOWN*0.1)
        pixel_cat = VGroup(cat_head, cat_ear_l, cat_ear_r, cat_eye_l, cat_eye_r, cat_smile)
        
        # Unit square grid representation
        # We define a localized coordinate system for the transformation math
        grid_origin = np.array([0, 0, 0])
        unit_square = Rectangle(height=1.0, width=1.0, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=2).move_to([0.5, 0.5, 0])
        
        # Background grid (visual only)
        bg_grid = VGroup()
        for i in range(-2, 4):
            bg_grid.add(Line([i, -2, 0], [i, 3, 0], color=color_grid, stroke_width=1))
            bg_grid.add(Line([-2, i, 0], [3, i, 0], color=color_grid, stroke_width=1))

        workspace = VGroup(bg_grid, unit_square, pixel_cat)
        # Position workspace in the C3 area as origin center
        self.place_in_area(workspace, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Adjust cat initial position relative to the local square
        # In setup, cat is at center of group, let's place it at 0.5, 0.5 locally
        pixel_cat.move_to(unit_square.get_center())

        self.play(FadeIn(bg_grid), Create(unit_square))
        self.play(FadeIn(pixel_cat))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_line_active)
        )
        
        # Matrix [[2, 1], [0.5, 1.5]]
        matrix = [[2, 1], [0.5, 1.5]]
        
        # Transformation animation
        # We manually transform the points to avoid apply_matrix complications with grid-placed groups
        def transform_point(p):
            # p is [x, y, z] relative to the world
            # Shift back to local origin (workspace center before transform was at B2-E5 center)
            center = self.grid["C3"] + [0.5, -0.5, 0] # Rough visual center estimate
            # More reliable: use the workspace's original center
            local_p = p - workspace.get_center()
            transformed_x = matrix[0][0] * local_p[0] + matrix[1][0] * local_p[1]
            transformed_y = matrix[0][1] * local_p[0] + matrix[1][1] * local_p[1]
            return np.array([transformed_x, transformed_y, 0]) + workspace.get_center()

        self.play(
            workspace.animate.apply_matrix(np.array([[2, 1], [0.5, 1.5]]).T),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_line_active)
        )
        # Emphasis on the stretched Pixel
        self.play(pixel_cat.animate.set_stroke(width=2, color=YELLOW), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(pixel_cat.animate.set_stroke(width=0, color=WHITE), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(color_line_active)
        )
        
        # Highlight transformed square area
        # The unit_square is now a parallelogram. We'll fill its interior.
        filled_area = unit_square.copy().set_fill(color_area, opacity=0.3).set_stroke(width=0)
        
        question_mark = Text("?", font_size=48, color=color_area)
        self.place_at_grid(question_mark, "C4")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(filled_area))
        self.play(Write(question_mark))
        
        # Pulse effect
        self.play(question_mark.animate.scale(1.3), run_time=0.5, rate_func=there_and_back)
        self.play(question_mark.animate.scale(1.3), run_time=0.5, rate_func=there_and_back)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(color_line_active)
        )
        
        # Generalizing: add a second shape (small circle) to show it scales too
        extra_shape = Circle(radius=0.2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(extra_shape, "D2")
        self.play(FadeIn(extra_shape))
        self.play(extra_shape.animate.apply_matrix(np.array([[2, 1], [0.5, 1.5]]).T))
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(question_mark), FadeOut(filled_area), FadeOut(extra_shape))
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title = "Prerequisite Knowledge: The Basis Vectors"
        lines = [
            "Basis vectors i-hat and j-hat define the unit square.", 
            "The matrix tells us where these vectors land.", 
            "Their new positions determine the transformation's resulting area."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Anchors and points
        origin = self.grid["D2"]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Basis vectors
        i_hat = Arrow(origin, self.grid["D3"], buff=0, color="#FF0000", stroke_width=4)
        j_hat = Arrow(origin, self.grid["C2"], buff=0, color="#00FF00", stroke_width=4)
        
        # Labels
        i_label = Text("i-hat", font_size=16, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(i_label, "E3")
        
        j_label = Text("j-hat", font_size=16, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(j_label, "C1")
        
        # Unit square
        unit_square = Rectangle(width=1, height=1, color="#FFFFFF")
        unit_square.set_style(stroke_width=2)
        unit_square = DashedVMobject(unit_square)
        self.place_in_area(unit_square, "C2", "D3")
        
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(i_hat),
            GrowArrow(j_hat),
            FadeIn(i_label),
            FadeIn(j_label),
            Create(unit_square),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Matrix components target positions
        # i-hat moves to (3,0) -> D5
        # j-hat moves to (0,2) -> B2
        target_i = Arrow(origin, self.grid["D5"], buff=0, color="#FF0000", stroke_width=4)
        target_j = Arrow(origin, self.grid["B2"], buff=0, color="#00FF00", stroke_width=4)
        
        # Labels target positions
        target_i_label = Text("i-hat", font_size=16, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(target_i_label, "E5")
        
        target_j_label = Text("j-hat", font_size=16, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(target_j_label, "B1")
        
        # Transformed rectangle
        # Rectangle starts at origin, width 3, height 2. Top-left B2, bottom-right D5
        transformed_rect = Rectangle(width=3, height=2, color="#FFFFFF")
        transformed_rect.set_style(stroke_width=3, fill_opacity=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(transformed_rect, "B2", "D5")

        self.play(
            Transform(i_hat, target_i),
            Transform(j_hat, target_j),
            Transform(i_label, target_i_label),
            Transform(j_label, target_j_label),
            ReplacementTransform(unit_square, transformed_rect),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Highlighting the final area
        area_text = Text("Area = 6", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(area_text, "C4") # Center of the transformed area
        
        self.play(
            transformed_rect.animate.set_stroke(color=YELLOW, width=5),
            Write(area_text),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final cleanup highlight
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define the lecture script
        lecture_lines = [
            'The determinant is the factor by which areas scale.', 
            "If it's six, every shape's area is now sixfold.", 
            "This value represents the transformation's geometric scaling power."
        ]
        
        # Initialize layout
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Determinant Geometrically", lecture_lines)
        
        # Matrix to be used for transformations: [[3, 1], [0, 2]]
        # In Manim's 3D coordinate system, we extend it with [0, 0, 1] for the z-axis.
        trans_matrix = [[3, 1, 0], [0, 2, 0], [0, 0, 1]]
        yellow_hex = "#FFFF00"
        blue_hex = BLUE_B
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color match for lecture text
        self.lecture[0].set_color(blue_hex)
        
        # Highlight a unit square area
        unit_square = Square(side_length=1.0, color=blue_hex, fill_opacity=0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(unit_square, "D3")
        
        # Label it 'Area = 1'
        label_1 = Text("Area = 1", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_1, "E3")
        
        self.play(
            Create(unit_square),
            Write(label_1),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Color match for lecture text
        self.lecture[1].set_color(yellow_hex)
        
        # Transform the square into a parallelogram using matrix [[3, 1], [0, 2]]
        # We create a new shape at origin, apply matrix, then place it at the same grid point
        parallelogram = Square(side_length=1.0, color=yellow_hex, fill_opacity=0.4)
        parallelogram.apply_matrix(trans_matrix)
        self.place_at_grid(parallelogram, "D3")
        
        # Animate the label 'Area = 1' changing into 'Area = 6' (#FFFF00)
        label_6 = Text("Area = 6", font_size=24, color=yellow_hex)
        self.place_at_grid(label_6, "E3")
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(unit_square, parallelogram),
            ReplacementTransform(label_1, label_6),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Color match for lecture text
        self.lecture[2].set_color(yellow_hex)
        
        # Clean up previous shapes
        self.play(FadeOut(parallelogram), FadeOut(label_6), run_time=0.8)
        
        # Draw a circle
        circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color=blue_hex, fill_opacity=0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "D3")
        
        # Transform it into an ellipse using the same matrix
        ellipse = Circle(radius=0.5, color=yellow_hex, fill_opacity=0.4)
        ellipse.apply_matrix(trans_matrix)
        self.place_at_grid(ellipse, "D3")
        
        # Display text 'Determinant = 6' at the top of the screen in #FFFF00
        det_label = Text("Determinant = 6", font_size=32, color=yellow_hex)
        self.place_in_area(det_label, "A2", "A5")
        
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(circle, ellipse),
            Write(det_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup Title and Lecture Lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Calculation: The 2x2 Formula", 
            [
                'For a 2x2 matrix, the formula is ad minus bc.', 
                "The product 'ad' represents the primary rectangular area.", 
                "Subtracting 'bc' corrects for the parallelogram's tilt.", 
                'This simple calculation yields the exact area scaling factor.', 
                "We use this value to understand the transformation's effect."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # Matrix creation using Text for compatibility
        m_a = Text("a", font_size=36)
        m_b = Text("b", font_size=36)
        m_c = Text("c", font_size=36)
        m_d = Text("d", font_size=36)
        lb = Text("[", font_size=60)
        rb = Text("]", font_size=60)
        
        matrix_vals = VGroup(
            VGroup(m_a, m_c).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5),
            VGroup(m_b, m_d).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)
        
        matrix_obj = VGroup(lb, matrix_vals, rb).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(matrix_obj, "B1", "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Formula creation
        f_a = Text("a", color="#00FFFF", font_size=40)
        f_d = Text("d", color="#00FFFF", font_size=40)
        f_minus = Text("-", color="#00FFFF", font_size=40)
        f_b = Text("b", color="#00FFFF", font_size=40)
        f_c = Text("c", color="#00FFFF", font_size=40)
        formula = VGroup(f_a, f_d, f_minus, f_b, f_c).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "E1", "F3", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_obj), FadeIn(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Visualize primary area 'ad'
        # Coordinates for unit vectors scaled by a and d
        # For symbolic representation, we just use a rectangle
        rect_ad = Rectangle(width=2, height=1.5, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(rect_ad, "B4", "F6", scale_factor=0.7)
        rect_label = Text("Area = ad", font_size=20, color="#FFFF00")
        rect_label.next_to(rect_ad, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(
            Create(rect_ad),
            Write(rect_label),
            m_a.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            m_d.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            f_a.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            f_d.animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        # Illustrate 'bc' tilt factor conceptually
        tilt_arrow = CurvedArrow(rect_ad.get_corner(UR), rect_ad.get_corner(UR) + RIGHT*0.5 + DOWN*0.2, color="#FF00FF")
        tilt_text = Text("bc tilt", font_size=18, color="#FF00FF")
        tilt_text.next_to(tilt_arrow, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            Create(tilt_arrow),
            Write(tilt_text),
            m_b.animate.set_color("#FF00FF"),
            m_c.animate.set_color("#FF00FF"),
            f_b.animate.set_color("#FF00FF"),
            f_c.animate.set_color("#FF00FF")
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Example: [[3, 1], [0, 2]]
        ex_a, ex_b, ex_c, ex_d = "3", "1", "0", "2"
        t_a = Text(ex_a, font_size=36, color="#00FF00")
        t_b = Text(ex_b, font_size=36, color="#00FF00")
        t_c = Text(ex_c, font_size=36, color="#00FF00")
        t_d = Text(ex_d, font_size=36, color="#00FF00")
        
        # Numerical Formula
        nf_a = Text(ex_a, font_size=40, color="#00FF00")

    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Scene
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Zero Case: Collapsing Dimensions", 
            [
                'A determinant of zero means the plane has collapsed.', 
                'The 2D grid squashes down into a 1D line.', 
                'All area is lost, making the transformation irreversible.', 
                'We cannot "un-squash" a line back into Pixel.', 
                'This zero case is vital for checking matrix invertibility.'
            ]
        )
        
        # Create Coordinate system mobjects
        # We'll build a custom grid to avoid NumberPlane overhead
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        for x in range(-2, 3):
            grid_lines.add(Line([x, -2, 0], [x, 2, 0], stroke_width=1, color=GRAY))
        for y in range(-2, 3):
            grid_lines.add(Line([-2, y, 0], [2, y, 0], stroke_width=1, color=GRAY))
        
        i_hat = Arrow([0, 0, 0], [1, 0, 0], buff=0, color="#00FF00")
        j_hat = Arrow([0, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], buff=0, color="#00FFFF")
        basis_group = VGroup(grid_lines, i_hat, j_hat)
        
        # Place the grid system in the designated area
        self.place_in_area(basis_group, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line 1: 'A determinant of zero means the plane has collapsed.'
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#ADD8E6") # Light Blue
        self.play(Create(grid_lines), GrowArrow(i_hat), GrowArrow(j_hat))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line 2: 'The 2D grid squashes down into a 1D line.'
        # Transformation: i -> (1,1), j -> (1,1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00") # Yellow
        
        # Matrix is [[1, 1], [1, 1]]
        target_i = Arrow(i_hat.get_start(), i_hat.get_start() + np.array([1, 1, 0]) * 0.8, buff=0, color="#00FF00")
        target_j = Arrow(j_hat.get_start(), j_hat.get_start() + np.array([1, 1, 0]) * 0.8, buff=0, color="#00FFFF")
        
        # Manually calculate transformation for grid lines to ensure they collapse to y=x
        collapsed_lines = VGroup()
        # Origin of the grid area for reference
        origin = basis_group.get_center()
        # Scale factor was 0.8 during placement
        s = 0.8
        
        # Each point (x,y) goes to (x+y, x+y) relative to origin
        for line in grid_lines:
            p1 = line.get_start() - origin
            p2 = line.get_end() - origin
            
            # Simple projection to y=x line
            new_p1_val = (p1[0] + p1[1])
            new_p2_val = (p2[0] + p2[1])
            
            collapsed_lines.add(Line(
                origin + np.array([new_p1_val, new_p1_val, 0]),
                origin + np.array([new_p2_val, new_p2_val, 0]),
                stroke_width=2, color=GRAY_B
            ))

        self.play(
            Transform(grid_lines, collapsed_lines),
            Transform(i_hat, target_i),
            Transform(j_hat, target_j),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line 3: 'All area is lost, making the transformation irreversible.'
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFA500") # Orange
        
        # Highlight the collapse - visual pulse on the line
        self.play(grid_lines.animate.set_stroke(width=4), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(grid_lines.animate.set_stroke(width=2), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Line 4: 'We cannot "un-squash" a line back into Pixel.'
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFB6C1") # Pink
        
        # Shake the line to indicate it's stuck/locked
        self.play(basis_group.animate.shift(RIGHT*0.1), run_time=0.1)
        self.play(basis_group.animate.shift(LEFT*0.2), run_time=0.1)
        self.play(basis_group.animate.shift(RIGHT*0.1), run_time=0.1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Line 5: 'This zero case is vital for checking matrix invertibility.'
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF0000") # Red
        
        # Add labels

outline.topic: The Determinant: The Magic Scaling Factor
outline.target_audience: University students (Introductory Linear Algebra) or Advanced High School students

sections.title: The Hook: The Morphing Canvas
sections.content: Introduce the concept of linear transformations as a way of stretching or squishing space. Use a character to visualize the change in a relatable way.
sections.example: Meet 'Pixel the Cat' sitting on a 1x1 square grid. As we apply a transformation matrix, the grid tilts and stretches. Pixel becomes taller and thinner. The Determinant is the answer to: 'How many times larger or smaller is Pixel's area now?'

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: The Basis Vectors
sections.content: Briefly review basis vectors (i-hat and j-hat) and how they define the unit square. Explain that a matrix simply tells us where these two vectors land after a transformation.
sections.example: Show i-hat (1,0) in red and j-hat (0,1) in yellow. They form a 1x1 square with an area of 1. If a matrix moves i-hat to (3,0) and j-hat to (0,2), the square becomes a 3x2 rectangle.

sections.title: Defining the Determinant Geometrically
sections.content: Formally define the determinant as the factor by which a linear transformation changes areas. Emphasize that if the determinant is 2, every shape in the plane now has twice the area it had before.
sections.example: An animation shows the unit square (area 1) transforming into a parallelogram. If the parallelogram's area is 6, the determinant of that transformation matrix is 6. This is the 'scaling factor' of the universe defined by that matrix.

sections.title: The Calculation: The 2x2 Formula
sections.content: Introduce the standard formula for a 2x2 matrix [a, b; c, d] as (ad - bc). Use a geometric overlay to show why this subtraction makes sense.
sections.example: Display a matrix [[3, 1], [0, 2]]. Calculate (3*2) - (1*0) = 6. Visually show a rectangle of area 6 being adjusted by the 'tilting' factor (the 'bc' part) to find the final area of the parallelogram.

sections.title: The Sign: Negative Determinants & Orientation
sections.content: Explain what it means when a determinant is negative. Introduce the concept of 'orientation' or 'flipping' the space.
sections.example: Pixel the Cat is looking to the right. After a transformation with a negative determinant, Pixel is mirrored and now looks to the left. It’s like flipping a sheet of paper over; the area is still positive, but the orientation is reversed.

sections.title: The Zero Case: Collapsing Dimensions
sections.content: Explore what happens when the determinant is exactly zero. This is a critical point for understanding matrix invertibility.
sections.example: If the transformation squashes the entire 2D plane down onto a single 1D line, the 'area' of the resulting shape is 0. Since the area is lost, the determinant is 0, and we can't 'un-squash' the line back into Pixel the Cat (the matrix is not invertible).

sections.title: Summary & Real-world Intuition
sections.content: Recap the three states: Positive (scaling), Negative (scaling + flipping), and Zero (collapsing). Connect this to how computer graphics engines calculate shadows or resize objects.
sections.example: A quick montage: A 3D dragon model being scaled up (Det > 1), a mirror reflection (Det < 0), and a shadow falling flat on the ground (Det = 0).

storyboard.title: The Calculation: The 2x2 Formula
lecture_lines: A 2x2 matrix defines the transformation’s movement.
The formula ad minus bc computes the scaling factor.
Calculating our example results in a determinant of six.
animations: Display matrix [[a, b], [c, d]] next to the parallelogram.
Show formula 'ad - bc' in #00FFFF; highlight 'ad' and 'bc' components.
Replace variables with 3, 1, 0, 2 and animate the result to 6.

storyboard.title: The Sign: Negative Determinants & Orientation
lecture_lines: Start with Pixel and our standard basis vectors.
A negative determinant mirrors Pixel to the other side.
Notice i-hat and j-hat have swapped their relative orientation.
This swap means we have flipped the entire space.
A negative sign indicates this fundamental change in orientation.
animations: Show 'Pixel' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pixel.svg] (#FFFFFF) facing right; label basis vectors i (red) and j (green).
Apply matrix [[-1, 0], [0, 1]]; 'Pixel' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pixel.svg] mirrors to face left.
Highlight that i is now to the left of j (flipped orientation).
Animate a circular arrow showing orientation direction reversing.
Display 'Negative Determinant = Flip' in #FF00FF.

storyboard.title: The Zero Case: Collapsing Dimensions
lecture_lines: Some transformations land both basis vectors on one line.
This collapses the entire plane, losing all area.
A zero determinant means the transformation is not invertible.
animations: Start with standard grid; animate i and j moving to (1,1).
Shrink all grid lines until they align perfectly on the line y = x.
Fade in red (#FF0000) text 'Area = 0' and 'Not Invertible'.

storyboard.title: Summary & Real-world Intuition
lecture_lines: Determinants scale, flip, or collapse our mathematical world.
Graphics engines use them to render shadows and reflections.
It is the fundamental scaling factor of linear algebra.
animations: Display three small grids side-by-side: scaled, flipped, and collapsed, enhanced with [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/shadows.svg] for depth.
Label them 'Det > 0', 'Det < 0', and 'Det = 0' respectively, alongside [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ref.svg] to indicate the transformation reference.
Morph all labels into 'The Magic Scaling Factor' in large yellow (#FFFF00) text.
